name: 46,XX Difference of Sex Development Induced by Maternal-Derived Androgen
aliases: Fetal Virilization Due to Maternal Androgen Excess

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Maternal Androgen-Induced 46,XX DSD

criteria.description: Presence of 46,XX karyotype without SRY gene
Evidence of elevated maternal androgen levels during pregnancy or maternal androgen-secreting tumor
Clinical signs of virilization in the female neonate including clitoromegaly and labioscrotal fusion
Normal fetal adrenal steroidogenesis excluding congenital adrenal hyperplasia
Exclusion of other causes of 46,XX DSD such as enzyme deficiencies or androgen insensitivity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of 46,XX karyotype, documented maternal androgen excess during pregnancy, and clinical virilization of the female neonate
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of congenital adrenal hyperplasia and other enzymatic defects.

pathognomonic.notes: Enlargement of the clitoris due to androgen exposure
Partial or complete fusion of the labia resembling scrotum
Ambiguous genitalia due to androgen exposure

common.notes: Increased size of clitoris beyond normal range
Commonly observed in virilized external genitalia
searchTerms: persistent common urinary and genital opening
single opening for urine and genitalia

common.notes: Increased fine hair growth due to androgen exposure

occasional.notes: Skeletal maturation accelerated by androgen exposure
Sensory changes reported in some cases

rare.notes: Hirsutism, deepening voice, or acne in mother
searchTerms: mother develops male traits in pregnancy

rare.symptomName: Psychosocial distress related to ambiguous genitalia
rare.notes: Emotional and social challenges in affected individuals
searchTerms: mental health issues due to genital ambiguity

rare.symptomName: Hypertension secondary to maternal androgen-secreting tumor
searchTerms: high blood pressure from maternal tumor
hypertension due to mother's androgen tumor

laboratory: Elevated maternal serum androgens (testosterone, androstenedione) during pregnancy
Normal fetal adrenal steroid profile excluding 21-hydroxylase deficiency
Normal electrolytes and cortisol levels in neonate
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing normal uterus and ovaries
No adrenal hyperplasia or tumors detected in fetus
genetic: Absence of mutations in CYP21A2, CYP11B1, or AR genes
other: Maternal history of androgen-secreting tumor or exogenous androgen exposure
Normal maternal adrenal imaging unless tumor present

distinguishingFeatures: Female external genitalia with undescended testes

redFlags: Ambiguous genitalia in a neonate with 46,XX karyotype
Maternal signs of androgen excess during pregnancy
Normal adrenal function excluding congenital adrenal hyperplasia
references: Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Arch Dis Child. 2006.
Lee PA, et al. Consensus statement on DSD. Pediatrics. 2006.
